overview: This one-page file index concerns the territorial sovereignty and legal status of the Kwantung Leased Territory. Its sole entry records a Departmental note emphasizing that the United States maintained a distinction between the legal status of the leased territory and that of the South Manchuria Railway Zone, and it directs the reader to another file concerning a communication to Japan associated with Neville.

subfiles.summary: This page is a file list containing a single entry for a note dated February 5, apparently filed in 1951. The note states that the Department consistently distinguished the legal status of the Kwantung Leased Territory from that of the South Manchuria Railway Zone. It also points to another file or document concerning communication no. 69 to Japan and mentions Neville.

interest: Although only an index page survives in the supplied text, it documents an important legal distinction in U.S. policy: the Kwantung leasehold and the South Manchuria Railway Zone were not treated as possessing the same status. The cross-reference may help a historian locate the substantive communication to Japan and trace how the State Department classified sovereignty questions involving former Japanese privileges in Manchuria.
